My time to shine! I'm a radiology resident and have to deal with this shit all the time. That "graininess" you see is due to a dearth of photons making it to the detector on the other side of the patient from the xray source. This severely degrades the quality of the images and makes interpretation challenging and sometimes impossible. Even on "plus sized" scanners that go up to 650+ pounds, you often cannot get enough radiation to the detectors to make good quality images.

There are also issues related to MRI and obese people, as they can get large enough to where the wavelength of the radio waves we send into their body cause constructive and destructive interference: http://radiopaedia.org/articles/dielectric-effect-artifact-2

Ultrasound can also be severely limited due to patient size, particularly of deep structures in the abdomen.
